subject: Initial-byte p99 regression — Acme Retail production spikes / CDN TLS retries
messages:
From: Ben Harvey <ben.harvey@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@redwood.ai; tina.zhou@cloudedge.net
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 09:14:22 -0700
Subject: Spike in initial byte p99 for /v1/generate — urgent

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp rise in first-byte latency (p99 ~ 2.1s, p95 ~ 850ms) for our API calls to /v1/generate starting ~07:45 PDT today. This has produced timeouts for some user flows and increased error rates. Our SLOs are being breached on the busiest product page.

Quick details:
- Region: us-west-2
- Client observed reattempts and TLS handshake errors in our agent logs (attached snippet).
- Overall throughput to Redwood is steady, but the spike seems to hit cold starts / initial token time.

We've opened an internal incident; can you confirm whether anything changed on your side (edge/CDN, routing, certs)? We need root cause and ETA for mitigation — this is impacting our checkout conversions.

Thanks,
Ben Harvey
VP Product, Acme Retail
ben.harvey@acme-retail.com
+1 415 555 0198

Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 09:48:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in initial byte p99 for /v1/generate — urgent

Quick diagnostic notes from infra: 
- Correlated traces show a 3x increase in TLS session renegotiation attempts hitting our edge clusters in us-west-2 at 07:42-07:58 PDT.
- Most retries surface before any application bytes are returned (initial byte latency).
- Upstream health shows a minority of requests receiving 502/524 from CloudEdge within the window.
- We see no concurrent model rollout or config change on our side.

I've attached an exported trace and a short table of p50/p95/p99 across the edge nodes (see attachments). Next step is to get CloudEdge to confirm whether there were certificate or peering flaps that would cause TLS renegotiations.

Sean Gallagher
SRE, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Attachments: acme_p95-logs-20260731.csv
From: Tina Zhou <tina.zhou@cloudedge.net>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Harvey <ben.harvey@acme-retail.com>
Cc: support@cloudedge.net
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 10:12:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in initial byte p99 for /v1/generate — urgent

Hi Marissa/Sean,

Thanks for CC'ing us. We see elevated TLS handshake error rates from a subset of upstream IP blocks tied to Redwood's origin in us-west-2 between 07:40-08:00 PDT. Preliminary find: a peering route churn with one of our POPs caused intermittent TCP resets, followed by client-side TLS retries that would delay initial byte delivery.

Action items on our side:
- We applied an emergency route stabilization at 08:05 PDT which reduced error counts.
- We'll provide a full trace and BGP/peering notes in the next 2 hours.

Tina
Tina Zhou
Account Ops, CloudEdge CDN
tina.zhou@cloudedge.net

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Harvey <ben.harvey@acme-retail.com>, Tina Zhou <tina.zhou@cloudedge.net>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 12:05:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in initial byte p99 for /v1/generate — urgent

Internal summary (for Marissa / execs):
- Root cause (probable): transient peering route churn at CloudEdge POPs in us-west-2 leading to TCP resets and TLS retries upstream. This manifested as elevated initial-byte p99 for customers routed through those POPs.
- Impact: Acme Retail p99 for first byte rose from baseline ~350ms to ~2.1s for a 16-minute window. Error rate (502/524) increased from 0.03% to 1.2% for the same window.
- Mitigation applied: CloudEdge route stabilization at 08:05 PDT; Redwood SRE rolled an emergency edge re-route for problematic upstream IPs at 08:12 PDT to avoid affected peering links. Both actions reduced p99 back to ~420ms by 08:20 PDT.
- Evidence: attached CSV of pXX across nodes and a trimmed TLS trace (cdn-trace-20260731.txt).

Next steps:
1) Post-incident: coordinate with CloudEdge on peer hardening and longer-term BGP session monitoring.
2) Product: consider a short client-side retry/backoff recommendation to reduce tail exposure during transient peering flaps.
3) CS: offer Acme a one-time SLA credit and a technical write-up for their SREs.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: cdn-trace-20260731.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Harvey <ben.harvey@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Tina Zhou <tina.zhou@cloudedge.net>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident update: initial-byte p99 regression (Acme) — actions and credits

Ben — update and next steps.

What happened: CloudEdge experienced a transient peering route churn in us-west-2 that caused TCP resets and upstream TLS retries for a subset of edge POPs. That led to elevated first-byte p99 for affected customers, including Acme, for ~16 minutes on 2026-07-31.

What we did:
- Coordinated with CloudEdge on emergency route stabilization (08:05 PDT) and applied an edge reroute from our side (08:12 PDT) to avoid impacted IP blocks.
- SRE team collected traces and validated p95/p99 returned to near baseline by 08:20 PDT.
- We captured logs and produced an incident packet and the CDN trace (links/attachments).

Compensation: We will apply a one-time service credit equal to 25% of July usage for the affected endpoints under DEAL-4382 and follow up with finance to process.

Proposed follow-ups (I will schedule):
- Joint postmortem with CloudEdge next Tue 08/04 10:00 PDT.
- Technical playbook for client retry/backoff and SRE runbook for BGP/peer flaps.
- Delivery of full incident packet (logs, traces, timeline) to Acme by EOD Mon 08/02.

Ben — apologies for the disruption. Let me know if you want a technical walk-through for your infra team; Karthik and Sean are available.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
